name: Bulgaria
basis: Закон за българското гражданство, чл. 15, ал. 1, т. 1 and чл. 15, ал. 2; Допълнителни разпоредби, §2, т. 1
quote_original: негов възходящ до трета степен включително
quote_translation: his ascendant up to the third degree inclusive
notes: Acquisition, not transmission at birth: art. 15(1)(1) waives the residence, income, language and release-of-prior-citizenship conditions for a person 'от български произход'. Origin itself is defined without a generational bound — §2(1) DR: 'Лице от български произход е лице, на което поне единият възходящ е българин' (a person at least one of whose ascendants is a Bulgarian). The ceiling recorded here comes from art. 15(2), which caps the documentary proof at an ascendant to the third degree inclusive; third degree in the direct line = great-grandparent. Both facts are in the instrument; the relations list reflects the art. 15(2) proof rule, which is the operative limit. Art. 8 is the ordinary parent rule. Verified by direct fetch; quote greps character-for-character against the Ministry of Justice page.

name: Hungary
basis: 1993. évi LV. törvény a magyar állampolgárságról, 4. § (3), as replaced by 2010. évi XLIV. törvény 2. § (2)
quote_original: akinek felmenője magyar állampolgár volt vagy valószínűsíti magyarországi származását
quote_translation: whose ascendant was a Hungarian citizen, or who makes his Hungarian origin probable
notes: Acquisition (kedvezményes honosítás / simplified naturalisation), not transmission at birth. 'Felmenő' = ascendant, with NO degree stated — no ceiling is written down, which is why unlimited stays false rather than true. Two distinct limbs in one clause: a citizen ancestor (descent-shaped) OR making Hungarian origin probable (origin-shaped), hence origin_based true. The 2010 amendment also removed the prior one-year Hungarian residence requirement and the 'magát magyar nemzetiségűnek valló' self-declaration that the 1993 as-enacted text carried. CAVEAT: njt.hu (Nemzeti Jogszabálytár, the official consolidated database) is unreachable from this network — TCP connection reset on both curl and WebFetch, IPv4 and www variants. The quote is taken from the amending act as published on the Parliament's law database; the CURRENT consolidated wording of 4. § (3) has not been re-verified against njt.hu.

name: Nigeria
basis: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, s.25(1)(a) and s.25(1)(b); s.26(2)(b); s.31
quote_original: of whose parents or any of whose grandparents is a citizen of Nigeria
quote_translation: of whose parents or any of whose grandparents is a citizen of Nigeria
notes: This is genuine citizenship BY BIRTH reaching a grandparent, not naturalisation: s.25(1)(b) makes a person born in Nigeria on or after independence a citizen by birth if either parent OR any grandparent is a citizen. s.25(1)(a) is the origin limb — born in Nigeria before independence, either of whose parents or any of whose grandparents 'belongs or belonged to a community indigenous to Nigeria', with a proviso that a parent or grandparent must have been born in Nigeria. s.26(2)(b) additionally lets a person of full age born OUTSIDE Nigeria any of whose grandparents is a citizen apply for registration (acquisition). s.31 back-dates parent/grandparent citizenship to independence. Grandparent is the furthest relation the text names anywhere in Chapter III. Verified by fetching the Federal Ministry of Justice PDF; quote is contiguous in the extracted text. PDF extraction whitespace may vary by extractor.

name: Poland
basis: Ustawa o repatriacji, art. 5 ust. 1 pkt 1 (definition of 'osoba polskiego pochodzenia'); Ustawa o Karcie Polaka, art. 2 ust. 1 pkt 3; Ustawa o obywatelstwie polskim, art. 30 ust. 1 pkt 7
quote_original: co najmniej jedno z jej rodziców lub dziadków albo dwoje pradziadków
quote_translation: at least one of her parents or grandparents, or two great-grandparents
notes: Explicit stated ceiling at great-grandparent, and asymmetric: ONE parent or ONE grandparent suffices, but TWO great-grandparents are required. Identical formula appears in Karta Polaka art. 2(1)(3). Origin turns on 'narodowość polska' (Polish nationality/ethnicity), not on the ancestor having been a Polish citizen — hence origin_based true. Acquisition, not transmission at birth: Polish origin or a Karta Polaka gets a permanent-residence permit, and art. 30(1)(7) of the citizenship act then allows recognition as a Polish citizen after one year's continuous residence on that permit. Separately, 'potwierdzenie posiadania obywatelstwa polskiego' (confirmation of citizenship) can reach arbitrarily far back by unbroken descent, but that is continuity of a citizenship never lost — no generational rule is stated for it, so it is not recorded here. Consolidated texts fetched from dziennikustaw.gov.pl (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 90 repatriation, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 76 Karta Polaka, Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1611 citizenship); byte-identical to the Sejm ELI API copies.

name: Slovakia
basis: Zákon NR SR č. 40/1993 Z. z. o štátnom občianstve, § 7 ods. 8 (and § 7 ods. 3); zákon č. 474/2005 Z. z. o Slovákoch žijúcich v zahraničí, § 2 písm. a) bod 2
quote_original: rodičov, prarodičov alebo praprarodičov bol československým
quote_translation: parents, grandparents or great-grandparents was a Czechoslovak [citizen]
notes: TWO separate limbs, both acquisition (grant of citizenship), not transmission at birth. (1) § 7 ods. 8, in force from 15 July 2026 and ABSENT from the 1 Jan 2022 consolidated version — citizenship may be granted without the 8-year residence condition to an applicant at least one of whose parents, grandparents or great-grandparents was a Czechoslovak citizen born on the territory of the Slovak Republic. Stated ceiling: great-grandparent. This limb is descent-based, not ethnic. (2) § 7 ods. 3 waives the residence condition for a holder of an osvedčenie Slováka žijúceho v zahraničí, and zákon 474/2005 § 2 písm. a) bod 2 defines that status as a person who keeps national consciousness and where 'on alebo jeho predok v priamom rade má slovenskú národnosť' — he OR HIS ANCESTOR IN THE DIRECT LINE has Slovak ethnicity. No degree is stated there; footnote 3 points to § 117 of the Civil Code, which only explains how degrees are COUNTED, it does not impose a cap. So the ethnic limb is ancestor_unspecified with no written cutoff — recorded as such, and unlimited stays false because the statute never says the chain is unbounded. Second source: https://static.slov-lex.sk/static/SK/ZZ/2005/474/20221201.html

name: Ukraine
basis: Закон України "Про громадянство України" № 2235-III, стаття 8 (набуття громадянства за територіальним походженням); Закон України "Про закордонних українців" № 1582-IV, стаття 1
quote_original: яка сама чи хоча б один із її батьків або її дід чи баба, прадід чи прабаба
quote_translation: who herself, or at least one of whose parents, or whose grandfather or grandmother, great-grandfather or great-grandmother
notes: The single most explicit generational text in this set: art. 8 names parents, grandparents AND great-grandparents by name, plus full/half siblings, children and grandchildren. The qualifying fact is TERRITORIAL, not ethnic — that ancestor was born or permanently resided before 24 August 1991 on territory that became Ukraine (or on listed predecessor-state territories: UNR, ZUNR, Ukrainian State, USRR, Zakarpattia Ukraine, UkrSSR, Crimean People's Republic, Crimean ASSR). Acquisition by application, not transmission at birth; conditions now include knowledge of the Constitution, Ukrainian history and the state language. Stated ceiling: great-grandparent. origin_based is true on account of the SECOND limb, a separate instrument: the Law on Foreign Ukrainians defines a закордонний українець by 'належність особи або її предків до української нації' (the person's or HER ANCESTORS' belonging to the Ukrainian nation) — ethnic, ancestor unspecified, no cap stated — and that status shortens the naturalisation residence requirement to one year. Second source: https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/1582-15/print

name: United Kingdom
basis: British Nationality Act 1981, s.3(2) and s.3(3)(b); s.2(1)(a); Immigration Rules Appendix UK Ancestry, UKA 4.1
quote_original: the father or mother of the parent in question
quote_translation: the father or mother of the parent in question
notes: Transmission at birth is capped at ONE generation abroad and the cap is STATED: s.2(1)(a) passes citizenship to a child born outside the UK only where the parent is a British citizen 'otherwise than by descent'. The grandparent appears only in an acquisition route — s.3(2) entitles a person born abroad to REGISTRATION while a minor where the parent was a citizen by descent and 'the father or mother of the parent in question' (i.e. the grandparent) was a citizen otherwise than by descent, subject to s.3(3)(c) requiring the parent to have spent 3 years in the UK with no more than 270 days' absence. Separately, Appendix UK Ancestry UKA 4.1 — 'The applicant must have a grandparent born in the UK or Islands' — is a work visa for Commonwealth citizens leading to settlement and then naturalisation; that is immigration with an ancestry condition, NOT descent. Second source: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-rules-appendix-uk-ancestry. Both quotes verified present.

name: Armenia
basis: Constitution of the Republic of Armenia, article 47, paragraphs 3 and 4; Law on Citizenship of the Republic of Armenia HO-16, article 13
quote_original: Հայաստանի Հանրապետության քաղաքացիություն կարող է ստանալ Հայաստանի Հանրապետության քաղաքացիություն չունեցող ազգությամբ հայ անձը
quote_translation: a person of Armenian ethnicity who does not hold citizenship of the Republic of Armenia may obtain citizenship of the Republic of Armenia
notes: A pure ORIGIN route with no generational axis at all: the qualifying fact is being 'ազգությամբ հայ' (Armenian by ethnicity), and art. 13 then disapplies the residence, language and Constitution-knowledge requirements of art. 13(1)(1)-(3). Constitution art. 47 para 3 gives ethnic Armenians the right to acquire citizenship from the moment they establish residence in Armenia, para 4 says they acquire it by a simplified procedure established by law. Acquisition, not transmission at birth. The ONLY relation the instruments name anywhere is 'parent' (art. 47 paras 1-2, and law art. 10 recognition limbs). I grepped the full consolidated law for Armenian ancestor terms — 'նախնի' (ancestor), 'պապ' (grandfather): zero hits; the 11 'տատ' hits are all substrings of 'հաստատող' etc. So no grandparent limb exists, and there is no ceiling to state because there is no chain. Proof of ethnicity runs partly through baptism certificates from a listed set of church bodies (art. 28). Constitution source (verified): https://www.president.am/hy/constitution-2015/

name: Cabo Verde
basis: Lei n.º 33/X/2023, de 22 de agosto, artigo 8.º, n.º 1, alíneas c) e e), as amended by Lei n.º 37/X/2024, de 22 de março; artigo 13.º, n.º 2, alínea b)
quote_original: O neto, bisneto ou trineto, de cabo-verdiano de
quote_translation: The grandchild, great-grandchild or great-great-grandchild of a Cabo Verdean [of origin]
notes: REACH RECORDED HERE IS UNDERSTATED BY THE SCHEMA. The text names 'trineto' — great-great-grandchild — so the qualifying ancestor may sit FOUR generations back, one further than the enum's great_grandparent can express. Read the relations field as parent/grandparent/great-grandparent PLUS great-great-grandparent. This is nacionalidade DE ORIGEM (attributed original nationality), not naturalisation, but alínea e) conditions it on a declaration ('se declarar que quer ser cabo-verdiano') filed with the Conservatória dos Registos Centrais; alínea c), the child limb, needs no declaration, only Cabo Verdean civil registration. Stated ceiling: great-great-grandparent, hence unlimited false. origin_based is false because the qualifying ancestor must be a 'cabo-verdiano de origem' — a national — not a member of an ethnic group; the closest origin-flavoured provision is art. 13.º(2)(b), which waives the residence requirement for naturalisation for those 'havidos como descendentes de cabo-verdianos' (regarded as descendants of Cabo Verdeans), unspecified degree. Both the 2023 principal law and the 2024 amendment were fetched from the official Boletim Oficial (INCV); 2023 text: https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/Download/4995

name: Kyrgyzstan
basis: Конституция Кыргызской Республики (2021), статья 51, часть 3; Закон "О гражданстве Кыргызской Республики", статья 14 часть 2 and статья 12 часть 5
quote_original: Каждый, доказавший свою принадлежность к народу Кыргызстана, имеет право приобрести гражданство Кыргызской Республики в упрощенном порядке.
quote_translation: Everyone who has proved their belonging to the people of Kyrgyzstan has the right to acquire citizenship of the Kyrgyz Republic under a simplified procedure.
notes: Origin route with no generational axis. The Constitution adds a second sentence giving Kyrgyz living outside the Republic the right to acquire citizenship by simplified procedure notwithstanding another citizenship. The citizenship law art. 14(2) admits 'лица, являющиеся этническими кыргызами' to citizenship with NO residence period and without the art. 13 conditions. Art. 12(5) is the one place ethnicity reaches into birth: a child born on Kyrgyz territory whose parents (or sole parent) are FOREIGN CITIZENS who are ethnic Kyrgyz is a citizen — ethnicity operating at birth through the parent, so the only relation named is parent. I grepped the full consolidated law for 'предк', 'дед', 'бабушк', 'прадед', 'происхожден': zero hits. No ancestor chain and therefore no ceiling. Acquisition, except art. 12(5) which is at birth. Law source (verified): https://cbd.minjust.gov.kg/api/v1/OpenData/GetDocument.json?Code=202103 — note the human-facing cbd.minjust.gov.kg pages are a JS app; the Ministry of Justice OpenData JSON endpoint is the fetchable official text.

name: Myanmar
basis: Constitution of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar (2008), section 345(a)
quote_original: person born of parents both of whom are nationals of the Republic of the
quote_translation: person born of parents both of whom are nationals of the Republic of the [Union of Myanmar]
notes: INCOMPLETE — origin_based false here means NOT ESTABLISHED, not established absent. Read it that way. What is established: s.345(a) of the 2008 Constitution requires BOTH parents to be nationals, and s.345(b) grandfathers existing citizens; s.346 delegates everything else to ordinary law. Parent is the only relation the Constitution names. What could NOT be established: the ethnic limb. The operative instrument is the 1982 Burma Citizenship Law (Pyithu Hluttaw Law No. 4 of 1982), whose s.3 confers citizenship on the listed national races settled in the territory before 1185 B.E. / 1823 A.D. — a date anchor rather than a generation count — and whose associate/naturalised categories turn on ancestors resident before 1948. I could not obtain that law from any official Myanmar government source: mlis.gov.mm (Myanmar Law Information System) returned no response at all (connection code 000), and the surviving *.gov.mm text I could reach is the archived President's Office constitution PDF cited above. The constitution quote is from a Wayback snapshot of the official president-office.gov.mm URL and is labelled as such. The 1982 law's origin rule is therefore left unrecorded pending an official source; it is not disproved. Note also that s.345 requires both parents to be nationals, which is narrower than the one-parent rule the repo's existing summary implies.

name: Rwanda
basis: Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda of 2003 revised in 2015, article 25; Organic Law nº 002/2021.OL of 16/07/2021 governing Rwandan nationality, article 2(2º) and article 6
quote_translation: All persons of Rwandan origin [and their descendants are, upon request, entitled to Rwandan nationality]
notes: Article 25 reads in full: 'All persons of Rwandan origin and their descendants are, upon request, entitled to Rwandan nationality.' — descendants, with no generational bound written anywhere. That is silence, not a grant of unlimited reach, so unlimited stays FALSE. The quote is clipped at 'origin' deliberately: PDF extraction inserts a double space between 'origin' and 'and', and the clause breaks across lines, so a longer quote would fail a character-for-character grep. The French column reads 'Toutes les personnes d'origine rwandaise et leurs descendants ont le droit d'acquérir la nationalité rwandaise' but uses U+201F apostrophes — avoid quoting it. Organic Law art. 2(2º) defines Rwandan origin RECURSIVELY: 'Rwandan origin: a relationship linking a person to Rwanda as a result of having one parent of Rwandan origin' — parent-of-a-parent-of-a-parent with no anchor date and no cutoff, which is why both parent and ancestor_unspecified are recorded. Art. 6 requires an applicant to be born to at least one Rwandan parent who is Rwandan 'by virtue of Rwandan ancestry' and to produce proof (testimony, a relative with nationality by origin, or other evidence of Rwandan origin). Mechanism is application/attribution on request, not automatic transmission. Contrary to a widely repeated claim, the 2015 Constitution contains NO 1959–1994 deprivation-restoration clause — I grepped the full gazette text for '1959': zero hits. Organic Law source (verified): https://www.migration.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/pdf_files/og_special_of_28.07.2021_ubwenegihugu_nyarwanda.pdf

name: Zambia
basis: Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act No. 2 of 2016, Article 37(1)(b); Article 36; Citizenship of Zambia Act No. 33 of 2016, section 17
quote_original: was born outside Zambia, has or had an ancestor who is,
quote_translation: was born outside Zambia, has or had an ancestor who is, [or was, a citizen]
notes: Article 37(1)(b) entitles a person over 18 born outside Zambia who 'has or had an ancestor who is, or was, a citizen' to apply to the Citizenship Board for REGISTRATION — but only after five years' ordinary residence in Zambia immediately preceding the application. 'Ancestor' is unqualified: no degree, no date anchor, no cutoff anywhere in Part on Citizenship. That is silence, so unlimited is FALSE, not true. Acquisition by registration, not transmission at birth. Separately worth recording for the map: Article 36 makes a person born outside Zambia a citizen by descent if at least one parent 'is or was a citizen by birth OR DESCENT' — so unlike the UK, the by-descent chain can itself pass on again indefinitely, though the only relation the article names is parent. The Citizenship of Zambia Act No. 33 of 2016 s.17 simply routes Article 37 applicants to the Board. Not origin-based: the qualifying ancestor must have been a citizen, not a member of a group. zambialii.org was avoided per the official-sources rule; text fetched from the National Assembly of Zambia. Act source (verified): https://www.parliament.gov.zm/sites/default/files/documents/acts/The%20Citizenship%20of%20Zambia%20Act%20No.%2033%2C%202016.pdf
